prompt:
You are a highly senior software engineer and architect with a focus on agentic development.

Evaluate the attached spec from a software design and architecture perspective:

Give it a score from 0 to 100, then defend your evaluation:

Do not be biased by who wrote it, an agent or a human, or by how fast it was developed.
Evaluate the material itself.

Compare it to its adjacents that might exist in the industry and have a big adoption already; e.g. 
Pydantic-AI, 
Claude's Agent SDK,
langchain/langgraph,

or whatever more relevant to what agentic_core is doing (top 2-3 competitors side-by-side would be great)

Provide criterion that you used to evaluate them.
note: A manual run: the person sent the prompt in each product and shared the conversation. Run 1 had no contract (no report format) and no sizes, so the score is in each answer's own words (only chatgpt.com's opens with a `Score: NN/100` line). All four pages show the same prompt, byte for byte, with agentic_core_spec.md attached. started_at is the time two pages show (chatgpt.com "Thursday 11:36 PM", gemini.google.com "October 1, 2026 at 11:36 PM"), read as the browser's local time, PDT (UTC-7), and converted; the pages show minutes, so the seconds are 00. claude.ai shows "2 days ago" and grok.com shows no time. finished_at is null: no page shows when an answer finished. repository_head is the commit that was agentic_core's default branch when the pages say the run began: 57f4a09, the repository's third commit (adding the spec, 2026-10-01 20:54:59 PDT), which stood until 6ff23cc at 23:48:30 PDT; its spec has 1,592 lines, and the claude.ai file chip reads 1,593 lines. The spec was attached as a file, so the commit is inferred from the times, not stated by a page. No page names the model of claude.ai or grok.com, or the effort of any site but chatgpt.com. `[redacted]` marks each place a conversation's address stood, in `url`, and, in chatgpt.com.md, the name the product addresses the person by and the name of another repository.

sessions.note: The page shows "Worked for 4m" and no model name; the effort is the label on the page's model picker in a signed-in view, so it is that picker's state when the page was read.
